I'd done something of the same essence with wanting to increase my KV cache pool in Ninfer. I had 262144 context using what was already there, but wanted 524288. I have a single 5090, so I decided on trying to reduce the quant of the kv cache to nvfp4, and was able to get it to work. I had 524k kv cache pool and it seemed to work fine. My only issue is the fact that Ninfer serve is not optimised for serving and is not mature as compared to vllm and slang, so when I would use it, there would be lane evictions of my main conversation if any tool call or subagent was launched by my harness. This is fine at lower context, but when you have 350-400k of context already this becomes a pain in the ass. Because the whole conversation needs to be prefilled again. Ultimately this is the reason I dropped Ninfer, and went back to vllm. I just did something similar in that, to support nvfp4 kv cache for sm120 and get a kv pool of 450k ish. I now don't use the full pool though, I cap it at 262144, and just leave the rest for subagents/tool call.

I did check with my current setup and p1p enabled driver with codex

    • This branch automatically enables P2P for --tp 2 --devices 0,1, and your current driver supports it.
    
      I checked your two RTX 5090s on driver 610.57.04:
    
      - Peer reads/writes: supported in both directions.
      - CUDA probe: canAccess=1 both ways; peer enablement and copies succeeded.
      - Measured bandwidth: 42.08 / 42.13 GiB/s.
      - Topology: PCIe NODE, through host bridges. That does not imply staging through host RAM.
    
      It uses NVIDIA’s CUDA Runtime (libcudart). NInfer implements its own collectives; the copy in src/ops/common/allreduce.cu:65 is:
    
      cudaMemcpyAsync(destination, source, bytes,
                      cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice, stream);
    
      With GPU pointers and peer access enabled, this supports direct GPU-to-GPU transfers. The function name does not need to contain Peer. NVIDIA documents this behavior.
    
      At TP2 startup, src/targets/qwen3_6/impl/runtime/program_impl.h:308 calls enable_peer_access(), which checks both directions and calls cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess() on each GPU.
    
      To repeat the probe I ran:
    
      nvcc -ccbin /usr/bin/g++-15 -arch=sm_120a -O2 \
        tools/tp2/p2p_probe.cu -o /tmp/ninfer-p2p-probe
      /tmp/ninfer-p2p-probe 0 1
    
      For a strict guarantee inside NInfer, the startup call should check its returned boolean and stop if it is false. Currently it discards that result, allowing silent host-staged fallback when peer access is unavailable.
    
      The probe verifies your system’s peer-copy support using cudaMemcpyPeerAsync; I have not traced an actual inference run. The README’s blanket “no P2P on GeForce” statement is outdated for your current setup.
